findings.title: Workflow inputs are interpolated directly into shell code
findings.description: The `mode`, `config`, and `focus` inputs are inserted into a multiline `run` script using `${{ inputs.* }}`. A crafted input containing shell syntax can break out of the quoted values and execute commands on the GitHub runner, where API keys and other workflow credentials are available.
findings.suggestion: Pass inputs through environment variables and quote them as data, or use an action that handles arguments without generating shell source. Validate mode and focus against allowed values.

findings.title: Audit gathering includes environment files that may contain live credentials
findings.description: The security focus explicitly gathers `**/*.env*` and `**/.env*`, then the runner sends gathered file contents to the configured AI provider. A normal `.env` containing production credentials can therefore be transmitted to a third party during an audit.
findings.suggestion: Exclude environment and secret files by default, add secret redaction before provider calls, and require an explicit opt-in with a clear warning to include them.

findings.title: File gathering can follow symlinks outside the repository
findings.description: `path.is_file()` accepts symlinks to regular files, and `read_text()` follows those links. A repository symlink matching an included pattern can cause files outside the configured repository (including local secrets) to be sent to the AI provider.
findings.suggestion: Resolve each candidate and verify it remains beneath the resolved repository root before reading it; consider skipping symlinks entirely.

findings.title: AI-generated Markdown is inserted unescaped into automatically created GitHub issues
findings.description: Finding titles, descriptions, and suggestions are incorporated directly into GitHub issue Markdown. Repository-controlled content can influence model output; if that output includes attacker-controlled links or remote images, enabling issue creation can publish them for maintainers to view and potentially leak viewer information.
findings.suggestion: Treat model output as untrusted: escape or sanitize Markdown, remove remote image embeds and unsafe links, and consider requiring review before publishing issue bodies.

findings.title: The action installs mutable code from the default branch
findings.description: The composite action installs the package from `git+https://github.com/atriumn/noxaudit.git` without a tag or commit pin. Each workflow run can therefore execute different code as the branch changes, making builds non-reproducible and increasing supply-chain exposure.
findings.suggestion: Install from a versioned release or immutable commit, and recommend consumers pin the action itself to a full commit SHA.

findings.title: Synchronous audit polling can wait forever
findings.description: `run_audit()` polls the batch API in an unbounded `while True` loop and sleeps for 60 seconds whenever the batch has not ended. A batch stuck in a nonterminal state leaves the CLI process—and any CI job—running indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add an overall deadline or configurable maximum wait, handle terminal error states explicitly, and return a useful timeout error.

findings.title: OpenAI synchronous batch polling has no timeout
findings.description: `run_audit()` also polls in an unbounded loop with a 60-second sleep. A batch that remains nonterminal can indefinitely consume a local process or CI runner.
findings.suggestion: Use a bounded polling deadline with backoff and report the batch ID and current status when the deadline expires.

findings.title: Gemini synchronous batch polling has no timeout
findings.description: `run_audit()` repeatedly retrieves the batch until it reaches a terminal state, with no deadline or maximum number of polls. A stuck job can hold a process or CI runner indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add bounded polling with backoff and surface failed, cancelled, and timeout states distinctly.

findings.title: The cost ledger is read and retained without a size bound
findings.description: `read_entries()` loads every JSONL entry into memory, and `get_last_n_days()` filters only after loading the complete file. The ledger grows on every audit and is never pruned, so status and cost summaries become progressively slower and more memory-intensive.
findings.suggestion: Prune entries beyond the retention period, or stream the file and retain only entries needed for the requested date range.

findings.title: Provider-specific model overrides are ignored when running audits
findings.description: Configuration parsing and `NoxauditConfig.get_model_for_provider()` support `providers.<name>.model`, and the documentation says those values override the global model. The runner instead constructs providers with `config.model` in its submit, retrieve, and synchronous paths, so the documented override is not used and cost tracking can record a model different from the one actually intended.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the model with `config.get_model_for_provider(pname)` consistently for provider construction, audit submission, retrieval, and cost tracking.

findings.title: Documented SARIF action input does not exist
findings.description: The guide configures `output-format: sarif`, but `action/action.yml` defines the input as `format`. GitHub Actions will not pass the undocumented input to the action, so following the guide leaves the action using its default Markdown format and prevents the documented SARIF behavior.
findings.suggestion: Change the examples and input table to use `format: sarif`, or rename the action input and update all consumers consistently.

findings.title: The documented action inputs and provider support do not match the action
findings.description: The input table lists `openai-api-key` and `google-api-key`, but neither input exists in `action/action.yml`; the action also installs the base package without the `openai` or `google` extras. Workflows following this reference cannot configure those providers through the action as documented.
findings.suggestion: Either add the provider inputs and install the corresponding extras, or document that the GitHub Action currently supports only the providers it actually installs and configures.

findings.title: The documented development install omits an extra required by the test suite
findings.description: The documented `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` command does not install the optional `mcp` extra, but `tests/test_mcp_server.py` imports `noxaudit.mcp.server`, which imports `mcp.server.fastmcp` unconditionally. Following the setup instructions can therefore make the full test suite fail during collection.
findings.suggestion: Include the MCP extra in the development test installation, or make the MCP tests optional and skip them when the extra is not installed.

findings.title: The test dependency set does not include the MCP package required for test collection
findings.description: MCP is declared only as an optional `mcp` extra, while the test suite imports the MCP server module directly. Installing the `dev` extra alone, as the contribution guide instructs, does not provide that dependency and can prevent the test suite from collecting.
findings.suggestion: Add MCP to a dedicated test/development dependency set, or guard and skip MCP tests when the optional extra is absent.

findings.title: GitHub issue creation has no test coverage
findings.description: `noxaudit/issues.py` invokes external `gh` commands, applies severity filters, deduplicates issues, and formats user/model-provided content, but no issue-creation tests are included. Regressions in filtering, command arguments, failure handling, or issue content can affect real repositories without detection.
findings.suggestion: Add tests with mocked subprocess calls for disabled configuration, threshold boundaries, existing issues, command failures, and generated issue contents.

findings.title: Telegram notification behavior has no test coverage
findings.description: `send_telegram()` handles credentials, HTTP requests, response failures, and error output, but no tests exercise these paths. In particular, network exceptions are not handled, which can abort a completed audit after reports have been written.
findings.suggestion: Add mocked HTTP tests for missing credentials, success, non-200 responses, and request exceptions; decide explicitly whether notification failures should fail an audit.

findings.title: The focus-area summary omits the testing focus
findings.description: The README says there are seven focus areas, but its Focus Areas table lists only six and omits `testing`, despite the code registering it and the surrounding documentation listing it.
findings.suggestion: Add the testing row to the README table.

findings.title: The changelog is duplicated in a second maintained location
findings.description: This file duplicates the root `CHANGELOG.md` content. The two copies can drift, leaving contributors and readers with inconsistent release history.
findings.suggestion: Choose one source of truth and include or link to it from the other location.
